section: Creating CI/CD solutions for applications using OpenShift Pipelines
job_statement: When I need to automate application build, test, and deployment workflows, I want to create a customized CI/CD solution using pipelines, so I can reduce manual effort and ensure consistent delivery processes.
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to deploy application changes
Reduce likelihood of deployment errors
Ensure consistent build and test processes across environments
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Creating CI/CD solutions for applications using OpenShift Pipelines, lines 64-76
notes: Main job covering the overall goal of creating CI/CD pipelines for applications

section: Working with OpenShift Pipelines in the Developer perspective
job_statement: When I need to create CI/CD pipelines for my application, I want to access pipeline creation options from the Developer perspective, so I can build automated delivery workflows integrated with my development process.
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to create a working pipeline
Reduce complexity of pipeline configuration
Ensure pipelines integrate with application lifecycle
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Working with OpenShift Pipelines in the Developer perspective, lines 1503-1512
notes: Main job covering pipeline creation in Developer perspective. Two primary approaches: Pipeline builder and From Git option.

section: Constructing pipelines using the Pipeline builder
job_statement: As an application developer, when I need to create a customized pipeline, I want to use the Pipeline builder with visual configuration, so I can construct pipelines using reusable tasks without writing YAML manually.
parent_job: Create CI/CD pipelines for my application
related_jobs: Search and add tasks from Tekton Hub
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to configure pipeline tasks
Reduce errors from manual YAML editing
Ensure access to reusable pipeline tasks from the cluster
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Constructing pipelines using the Pipeline builder, lines 1522-1606
notes: UI-based approach using Pipeline builder. Supports both visual builder and YAML view. Requires Tekton Hub for full task catalog access.

section: Constructing pipelines using the Pipeline builder
job_statement: As a cluster administrator, when I want to enable developers to access curated tasks, I want to install and deploy a local Tekton Hub instance, so developers can search, install, and upgrade tasks directly from the console.
parent_job: Create CI/CD pipelines for my application
related_jobs: Link Tekton Hub to OpenShift cluster
desired_outcomes: Ensure developers have access to curated task catalog
Minimize dependency on public Tekton Hub
Reduce likelihood of using untrusted tasks
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Constructing pipelines using the Pipeline builder, lines 1535-1539
notes: Related job for administrators to enable developer self-service. Without local Tekton Hub, developers only access namespace tasks and public hub tasks.

section: Creating OpenShift Pipelines along with applications
job_statement: As an application developer, when I am deploying a new application from Git, I want to create pipelines using templates during application import, so I can establish CI/CD automation from the start without separate pipeline creation steps.
parent_job: Create CI/CD pipelines for my application

Ensure pipelines are automatically linked to application
Reduce steps required to enable CI/CD
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Creating OpenShift Pipelines along with applications, lines 1615-1627

section: Adding a GitHub repository containing pipelines

section: Enabling the manual approval gate controller
job_statement: When I need to implement approval gates in my CI/CD pipelines, I want to enable the manual approval gate controller, so I can ensure critical deployments require human authorization before proceeding.
parent_job: Control pipeline execution with manual approval gates
prerequisites: Have administrator permissions for openshift-pipelines namespace
Have cluster access via oc CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to enable approval capability
Ensure approval controller is ready before pipeline execution
Reduce likelihood of deploying without required authorization
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Enabling the manual approval gate controller, lines 5787-5834
notes: Technology Preview feature. This is a prerequisite configuration step before approval tasks can be used in pipelines.

section: Specifying a manual approval task
job_statement: When I need to control when pipelines proceed to critical stages, I want to configure approval tasks with specific approvers and thresholds, so I can ensure the right stakeholders authorize production deployments.
parent_job: Control pipeline execution with manual approval gates
prerequisites: Enable the manual approval gate controller
Create groups and add required users for group approval
desired_outcomes: Minimize configuration errors when defining approval gates
Ensure correct number of approvals required
Reduce likelihood of unauthorized deployments
Ensure approval timeout prevents indefinite pipeline blocking
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Specifying a manual approval task, lines 5842-6076
notes: Supports multiple approval patterns: multi-user approval (requires N approvals from individual users), group-based approval (requires approvals from group members), and mixed user/group approval. Default timeout is 1 hour.

section: Approving a manual approval task by using the web console
job_statement: When a pipeline reaches an approval gate that lists me as an approver, I want to approve or reject the task via the web console, so I can authorize or block critical deployments without using CLI tools.

Have a pipeline run waiting at an approval gate
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to locate pending approvals
Reduce likelihood of missing approval notifications
Ensure approval decisions are recorded with reason
Minimize errors when approving or rejecting
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Approving a manual approval task by using the web console, lines 6106-6131
notes: Web console provides notifications when approval is required. Multiple access points: notification link, Pipelines Approvals tab (Administrator and Developer perspectives), PipelineRun details window.

section: Approving a manual approval task by using the command line

Have a pipeline run waiting at an approval gate

evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Approving a manual approval task by using the command line, lines 6145-6209
notes: opc CLI is available in same package as tkn CLI. Supports list, describe, approve, and reject operations. Optional -m parameter for adding approval/rejection message.

section: Behavior of ApprovalTask with groups and users

parent_job: Control pipeline execution with manual approval gates

desired_outcomes: Minimize confusion about group approval behavior
Ensure approval policies match organizational requirements
Reduce likelihood of misconfiguring mixed user/group approvals
Understand how individual group member approvals are tracked
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Behavior of ApprovalTask with groups and users, lines 6218-6286
notes: Controller automatically tracks individual approvals from group members and updates group approval state. Supports complex policies combining individual users and groups.

section: Using Red Hat entitlements in pipelines
job_statement: When building container images in pipelines that require RHEL packages, I want to use Red Hat entitlements, so I can access RHEL repositories during the build process.
prerequisites: Enable the Insights Operator feature on the OpenShift cluster
Configure importing of Red Hat entitlements into the Insights Operator from Simple Content Access (SCA)
Log in to the OpenShift cluster using the oc CLI
related_jobs: Build container images using Buildah task
desired_outcomes: Minimize time required to configure entitlement access
Reduce likelihood of build failures due to missing RHEL packages
Ensure entitlements are securely managed across pipeline namespaces
Avoid manual secret management overhead
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Using Red Hat entitlements in pipelines (abstract and overview), lines 6358-6368
notes: This main job has two distinct user stories for different implementation approaches: manual secret copying (simpler, for few namespaces) vs CSI driver (automated, for many namespaces).

section: Using Red Hat entitlements by manually copying the etc-pki-entitlement secret
job_statement: When I have a limited number of pipeline namespaces and need RHEL entitlements for builds, I want to manually copy the etc-pki-entitlement secret to each namespace, so I can provide entitlements without additional operator configuration.
parent_job: Use Red Hat entitlements in pipelines
prerequisites: Install the jq package on your system
Configure importing of Red Hat entitlements into the Insights Operator
Verify that the etc-pki-entitlement secret exists in the openshift-config-managed namespace
related_jobs: Configure Buildah task to use rhel-entitlement workspace
desired_outcomes: Minimize complexity of entitlement setup for simple use cases
Reduce dependencies on additional operators
Ensure entitlement secret is correctly formatted in target namespace
Complete entitlement setup in under 5 minutes for small deployments
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Using Red Hat entitlements by manually copying the etc-pki-entitlement secret, lines 6412-6493
notes: Recommended when there are a limited number of pipeline namespaces. Requires jq for JSON manipulation.

section: Using Red Hat entitlements by sharing the secret using the Shared Resources CSI driver operator
job_statement: When I need RHEL entitlements across many pipeline namespaces, I want to automatically share the etc-pki-entitlement secret using the Shared Resources CSI Driver, so I can avoid manual secret copying and ensure consistent entitlement access.
parent_job: Use Red Hat entitlements in pipelines
prerequisites: Log in to the OpenShift cluster as a user with cluster administrator permissions
Enable the Shared Resources CSI Driver operator on the cluster
Configure importing of Red Hat entitlements into the Insights Operator
Verify that the etc-pki-entitlement secret exists in the openshift-config-managed namespace
related_jobs: Manage service account permissions for pipelines
Configure Buildah task to use rhel-entitlement workspace
desired_outcomes: Minimize manual secret management overhead across multiple namespaces
Reduce likelihood of entitlement configuration drift between namespaces
Ensure automatic entitlement availability for new pipeline namespaces
Centralize entitlement secret management
evidence: create-combined.adoc -> Using Red Hat entitlements by sharing the secret using the Shared Resources CSI driver operator, lines 6501-6628
notes: Requires cluster admin permissions. Recommended when using the Shared Resources CSI Driver. Creates SharedSecret CR with RBAC.
